semantic_operation: scale to integer permyriads/hundredths; nearest ties positive at quantum1; divide by100
required_checks: Use native nearest_ties_positive; do not return source add-half/floor result.
Validate the actual scaled rounding operand, including bypass/lazy-path behavior.
Selected-domain source proof must establish intrinsic5, cap100, bonus100 and no active Weakness or other numeric suppliers.
Changed positive suppliers require their own bounded exactness proof; selected output samples cannot grant it.
proof: All checks apply to the actual binary64 scaled operand. Existing multiplication and division remain in source order; this does not prove arbitrary upstream real-number or reducer parity.
For 0 <= x <= the second predecessor of 0.5, x+0.5 cannot round up to1; both results are0. The immediate predecessor of0.5 is deliberately excluded.

For 0.5 <= x <= 2^52, representable neighbors below a half boundary are far enough from its following integer that adding0.5 cannot round across that integer; actual half ties select the larger integer. The upper endpoint remains unchanged.
For -1 <= x <=0, subtraction/cancellation with0.5 cannot cross a floor boundary except at the actual half tie; both round to the same integer.

For -2^52 <= x <=-1, adding0.5 decreases magnitude. The result spacing is no larger than input spacing, so a representable neighbor of a half boundary cannot be rounded across its following integer. Exact negative half ties select the larger integer.
The outside odd integers +(2^52+1) and -(2^52+1) demonstrate why the magnitude limits are availability guards. No source arithmetic discrepancy becomes a native rule.
Each native nearest rounding is quantum1 on the scaled quantity followed by division by100, rather than quantum0.01 division that would change the binary scale operation.
